_doc: GOV-PD-1108 (owner 2026-11-08: "US .gov sites should always 'be fair game' for our purposes"). Read only by vera/gov_public_domain.py. LICENCE STATUS ONLY, never access: robots.txt (read first), TDM reservations, Content-Signal/noai, site terms, the deny list, rate limits, Crawl-delay and the API allowlist all still apply unchanged, before this rule is ever consulted. Legal basis: 17 U.S.C. 105 (no US copyright in a work of the United States Government, i.e. prepared by a federal officer or employee as part of official duties). Rule 'us-federal-public-domain' applies to a page ONLY when (1) its host is, or is a subdomain of, a domain in the vendored CISA dotgov-data snapshot whose Domain type is federal (dataset.federal_types), or of a zone in federal_zones_outside_gov; (2) it is not under exclude_hosts; (3) the page declares no licence of its own and none of the page_override signals (copyright notice, third-party text credit, contractor or grantee statement) is present; (4) the snapshot is not older than dataset.max_age_days. State, city, county, tribal and other non-federal .gov hosts get NO automatic public domain: they go through the normal licence gate. The granted licence is the existing owner-approved allowlist entry LicenseRef-us-government-work (config/licence_allowlist.json). mode: off (nothing computed) | shadow (computed and recorded in dev/trace fields only; no decision changes) | on (missing-licence federal pages are allowed by vera.licence_gate and web pages carry the licence). Ships shadow (orchestrator 2026-11-08); on follows after the shadow counts are reviewed. Research and quotes: work/GOV-PD-1108/research.md.
_calibration_note: max_age_days 180 is a SAFETY bound, not a decision threshold: CISA updates the files daily when there is activity (README, read 2026-11-08); federal-type churn is low, and a stale snapshot only fails closed (rule not applied). Data seen: one snapshot of 2026-11-08 (row counts in the snapshot file). What would change it: a refresh diff showing federal domains changing type or registrant within 180 days -> shorten. The page_override markers are an uncalibrated, narrowing-only heuristic: a hit only removes the public-domain status (the page falls back to the normal licence gate, i.e. it is treated as before this rule); a miss is bounded by exclude_hosts and the image-credit rule. Measured on synthetic fixtures and one real page summary (energy.gov DOE Explains, image credit only). Calibrate from shadow-mode dev counts (gov_pd reason codes) before mode on.

dataset.refresh: python3 -B -I scripts/refresh_us_gov_domains.py (one fetch through vera.public_fetch: robots.txt first, pinned public address, byte caps); review the printed diff, then commit the snapshot as a normal batch

federal_zones_outside_gov.note: 17 U.S.C. 105 covers works of military officers and employees in official duties; academy and war-college faculty scholarly works are an exception (Compendium 313.6(C)(1)); page_override still applies

federal_zones_outside_gov.evidence: RFC 1480 section 2 (read 2026-11-08): "This branch may be used for agencies of the federal government."
federal_zones_outside_gov.note: e.g. USDA Forest Service legacy hosts

exclude_dataset_rows.reason: DOE rows are admitted ONLY when the Suborganization names a DOE office or a power/information administration (full match). Everything else, including every national laboratory, NREL, NERSC, ORAU, Jefferson Lab (cebaf.gov), Hanford and Savannah River contractors, NNSS/LLC rows, the isotope center and rows with no suborganization, is excluded: contractor-operated (M&O) or unknown. Narrowing only; derived from the dataset's Suborganization column (opus review GOV-PD-1108 finding 1). Contractor status is background knowledge: research.md caveat C2.

Narrowing only.

page_override._doc: Scanned only on the page's visible text (and its declared rel=license link), only to REMOVE public-domain status. Case-insensitive regexes. image_credit_patterns are recorded (image_credit=true) but do NOT cause fallback: VERA-DAR uses page text only and never an image, so an image credit governs the image, not the text (DOE web policies: some images 'may have been obtained from other organizations'). A third-party hit is ignored only when it lies INSIDE an image-credit match itself (e.g. the 'courtesy of' of 'Image courtesy of X'); any other 'courtesy of', credit, wire-service or syndication marker falls back (opus review finding 4). A textual licence statement (Creative Commons, CC BY..., 'licensed under') is a declared licence: the page falls back to the normal licence gate, so an ND licence is never bypassed.
